To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the new physics parameters can be measured by studying pairs of decays which are SU(3) related in the SM, that this allows us to rule many NP models, and that this is possible without the knowledge of NP strong phases.

the new physics in b ¯ →s ¯ penguin decays can be described in terms of four effective amplitudes, that the weak phases of these amplitudes can be measured in time-dependent measurements of pairs of related decays, that the amplitudes themselves can be measured in a variety of ways, and that the amplitu- des and phases can be used to rule out many models of new physics.

the time-dependent measurement of two B decays, one with large b > s ¯ penguins and one without penguins, allows one to measure the new-physics parameters A NP q (q = u, d, s, c) and the weak phases Φ q, thus allowing one to rule out many new-physics models.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NP parameters A u, d, c and  Φ u, d, Φ c are small, but non-zero, and that the NP parameters  A s and  Φ s are zero within the present experimental accuracy.
there is no new physics in b ¯ → q ¯ penguin decays, or, if it exists, that it is of the kind described by the model-independent parametrizations we have considered.
the new physics has to be a combination of a new weak phase and a new strong phase, both of which are small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NP effects in B ¯ → K ¯ ( K, π ) and B s ¯ → D s ¯ ( D s, K ) decays are described by two effective amplitudes with two phases.
we have developed a method to identify NP in b → s penguin decays, and we have shown that this method is very powerful in ruling out a number of NP models.
the time-dependent CP asymmetry measurements in neutral B meson decays can be used to identify new physics in the flavour sector of the Standard Model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a measurement of the time-dependent CP asymmetry in the B s ¯ → K ∗ 0 K ∗ 00 decay, which has a large b > s ¯ penguins and a negligible b ¯ –> d ¯ penguins amplitude, allows us to determine the new physics contributions in B s ¯ –> K ¯ K ∗  and B s ¯ ¯ ¯ –> φ φ.
the NP effects in B penguin modes can be measured with a high precision.
a measurement of the time-dependent CP asymmetries in a few B decays can allow us to determine the new physics parameters and thus rule out many NP models.
